notes: - Incoming voice notes: the file itself was the problem — two layers of it. 1.1.19's capture worked (the assistant had the file), but the answering model was OpenRouter, not Gemini — the Activity log's brain.switch line showed why: 'Switched from 'Gemini 1' to 'OpenRouter 1': error 400: Unable to process input: the file or media data is empty, corrupted, or malformed.' Gemini was tried first and refused the file itself. Layer one: when a voice note plays, Google loads the sound in ranged pieces (HTTP 206); the capture kept the biggest single piece and called it the file — a fragment of an m4a, which is exactly 'corrupted or malformed'. The pieces are now put back together by their byte ranges, and only a complete file (a whole download, or pieces covering every byte) is ever handed over; if the pieces never complete, the failure line says how many bytes arrived of how many. Layer two: even a whole m4a is a format the models refuse, so every incoming voice note is now converted to MP3 once, when it is saved (ffmpeg; the original is kept when conversion is impossible). MP3 is what Gemini opens reliably — and OpenAI-style models can take an MP3 voice clip too, so they become a real hearing backup instead of answering 'I can't open it'.
